claim.scope: Exact-checkpoint three-segment native DiT continuation, four updates per segment, shared scene prompt and one unused donor. No decoded video or general prompt editing.
claim.text: A bounded native B-noise fork preserves A and regenerates B/C identically with or without a restart after the new B.

evidence.signal: All eight B/C updates and all 829440 timeline F32 values match edited continuous/split restart bitwise. A/future suffix unchanged; B and C nonvacuously changed; all parent checkpoint digest links authenticate.
Actual edited post-B state is rejected by base and other-donor branches with a contract mismatch before model setup; no output artifacts.
Unedited full timeline is bitwise equal to the prior native exact three-segment control.
Pinned upstream temporal gather/scatter AST expressions match tiny native GPU fixture with max error 0; RoPE check is source-level global-offset contract only.
48 Crystal examples: 11 segment edit/admission plus 37 history/timeline/exact/compact resume.
37 Python resume comparator tests including the new edit lineage/capture/counter mutation cases.
10 Python tiny-GPU-reference validation and mutation tests.
Rehashed source/checker/binary pins, five native guards and command receipts pass; no instrumented preterminal GPU readback/wait or encode allocation.

limitations: No decoded video or perceptual edit-quality assessment.
Full BF16/CUDA/Magi upstream neural parity not established; upstream refresh is temporal slicing and source-level RoPE offset only.
Real edit matrix is exact only; QBit stale-contract rejection is covered by focused Crystal specs.
Model uses one shared scene prompt; per-segment prompt edits, arbitrary new seeds and multiple edits remain unimplemented.
A latent immutability does not imply the last 20 A pixel frames remain unchanged with overlapping decoding.
Instrumented allocation counters exclude opaque MPS allocations; sampled guards cannot bound between-sample spikes.
Cache-aware headroom estimates reclaimability; no benchmark speedup claim from ordered runs.
Checkpoint semantics rely on the authenticated native producer; arbitrary self-consistent forged states are outside scope.
All large artifacts are local-only; digests do not provide recovery.
reason: Support a new take without recomputing the retained prefix or accidentally consuming a stale descendant history.
refresh: Use fresh external outputs. Rebuild and pin sources/executable, run focused specs and tiny native GPU/upstream slicing, repeat bounded parent/original/edited/split runs under the 30GiB/10%/64MiB/900s guards, authenticate all captures and checkpoint links, rerun stale-branch rejection and default regression. Use docs for commands.
risk: CAUTION: checkpoint branch identity and GPU temporal-source selection. Model arithmetic and tolerances unchanged.
rollback: Omit the paired opt-in noise-edit flags and continue the original branch with its matching states. Original files are never rewritten. Reverting this commit restores the former interface; strict executable/source binding disallows cross-build state reuse.
